messages.subject: How is imputation actually done?
parts:
Dear all,

I am looking for information on how INLA (and R-INLA) handles missing data in the response. Are the predictions computed integrating over the different posterior marginal distributions or over the joint posterior of the parameters? I'd say it is computed using the different posterior marginals of the (hyper)parameters but I am not sure.

Also, is there any document where this is explained in more detail?

Many thanks,

Virgilio

Hi

missing data in the response (NA) means simply no likelihood
contribution. Nothing is imputed.

This describes the interpretation of NA

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-does-inla-deal-with-NA-s-in-the-data-argument-


oops: the predicted values at locations with NA response, need to know
of the link function, unless the identity link is used, see

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-can-I-do-predictions-using-INLA-
